$comment: #692 STRUCTURE-ONLY CHANGES OF THE REPORT QUERIES, DECLARED (owner 2026-10-19: "let every report carry the generated output block (one-time fingerprint change), plus the bucket filter on the two Defender recommendation reports (also a one-time fingerprint change)" -> "Yes, both, in one release"). A report's fingerprint (Get-RAReportQueryFingerprint) hashes its query as authored, so such a change gives every report a new one -- and a finding that leaves a report whose fingerprint changed closes as 'report changed'. Per change: what it wrote, so Risk Analysis can compute the fingerprint the report had BEFORE it (Get-RAReportQueryFingerprintCarry) and store it with the verdict (sidata.RaReportStatus QueryHashCarry). The finding lifecycle and the close loop read a fingerprint that carries the one at a finding's last sighting as UNCHANGED: FirstDetected and history stay, nothing closes as 'report changed' or 'remediated' because of the change. removeBlocks (every report): generated blocks the change added (//__<name>_BEGIN__ ... //__<name>_END__). reports.<name>.restoreText: { now (the text the change wrote), was (what it replaced) }, white space made one. A change is never edited after it shipped: a later change is a new item. tests/pester/SIv3-ReportFingerprintCarry.Tests.ps1 proves, for every report, that the carry of the query today is the fingerprint the query had before the change (tests/pester/fixtures/report-fingerprints-before-692.json).

changes.description: Every report carries the generated data-out block; the two Defender recommendation reports carry the bucket filter (one slice per hash of the resource), and the Summary builds its owners with an extend so a group the slices split is merged into one row again. No row and no output column changes.

changes.description: The two CVE reports read Defender vulnerability management only for the devices of the slice being asked (_sliceTvmDevices, the same key and hash as the slice filter on the union) before the joins, instead of the whole table in every slice. The rows are the same: the slice filter at the end already kept only those devices; without slices the filter is a no-op. No row and no output column changes.

restoreText.now: // #880 -- THE SLICE'S OWN DEVICES: vulnerability management is read for the devices of THIS slice only (the same key // and hash as the slice filter on the union below), so a slice reads its own share of the table, not all of it before // the joins. Without slices the block is a no-op and every device is kept -- the rows are the same either way. let _sliceTvmDevices = DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities | summarize by DeviceKey = tolower(tostring(DeviceId)) //__BUCKET_FILTER_BEGIN__ | where 1 == 1 //__BUCKET_FILTER_END__ | project DeviceKey; let _TvmOnly = DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities | where tolower(tostring(DeviceId)) in (_sliceTvmDevices)

changes.description: The two managed-identity attack-path reports give a target no CI links the tier of its own resource tree: its top-level resource's CI, else its subscription's most critical CI (12,052 findings had no tier at the largest install). The rows and their keys are the same; only the tier column is filled -- so a finding last seen before this change is the same finding, never closed as report changed.
